quote: We live in an HOA, so we cannot put panels on the front of the house.
stewart_read: Customer proactively surfaces a potential gate; rep handles it as a solvable logistics point rather than a disqualifier, keeping the lead alive.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as an objection/DQ attempt, but customer isn't resisting the appointment, just disclosing a fact — not a stall.
coaching_implication: Good instinct to reassure rather than treat as blocker; could be sharpened by naming the HOA team by name for extra legitimacy.

quote: it wasn't that the deal was terrible, but it was just that lack of transparency.
stewart_read: Customer names the exact prior company behavior that killed the last deal (hidden tax implications of a rebate) but rep never asks which company or what specifically was hidden.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged probing further as scope creep into a competitor debate; but the schema calls this a probe miss since customer was still cooperating.
coaching_implication: Ask 'what company was that, so I know what to watch out for on our end' — turns disclosure into rapport and a legitimacy differentiator.

quote: I have an electric car. So that would be, something that I'm and it's a Tesla, so I like the brand.
stewart_read: Customer self-identifies as an EV owner interested in battery storage — a strong upsell/battery-fit signal.
coaching_implication: Rep acknowledged warmly ('Tesla's a good brand') but didn't flag this explicitly for the closer as a battery-priority lead; should be surfaced in the handoff, which it was, loosely, via 'have that conversation about the battery.'

quote: Okay. So I'm gonna send you a text from just my personal number.
stewart_read: Rep exposes a personal phone number to collect the bill photo, the exact anti-pattern the schema flags for privacy/security review.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive workaround given no automated capture tool exists yet, not a rep failure per se.
coaching_implication: Flag for floor-wide review per schema's detection_today directive; not a coachable rep error but a process gap to escalate.

quote: Yeah. We can definitely help get that up get that down quite a bit.
stewart_read: Rep captures the bill number and offers only a generic savings acknowledgment — capture without emotional flip against the utility.
coaching_implication: Should have flipped: 'so Santee Cooper is costing you $2.25-2.50 a month for a home you've had for 19 years — that's the number solar replaces' — tie the pain to the specific figure.

quote: and then we we will see you
stewart_read: Button-up skips the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake and the no-driving line is compressed/unclear before drifting into 6 minutes of travel talk.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the customer's easy acceptance ('That works. Sure.') as sufficient handshake; but schema treats this as a distinct required element.
coaching_implication: Always land the explicit fairness question before letting the call relax into rapport chat — locks the commitment procedurally.
